subject: MAP proposal: test artifact barter, narrow-scope prompt pack & takedown schedule

Cc: joe.patel@optiretail.com
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 10:19:00 -0700
Subject: MAP & sample assets for pilot evaluation

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. OptiRetail is excited to scope a short pilot to validate recall/slot-filling quality on our merchandising prompts. We discussed a mutual action plan (MAP) to exchange a small prompt pack + test cases so both sides can run the acceptance evals.

Quick context: we can share a ~150-case prompt pack (sanitized) and need a committed takedown window and strict usage constraints (no indexing, ephemeral only, audit log retention for 90 days). Procurement (Joe) will need a one-page MPA or SOW outlining timelines and data handling.

Can Redwood propose a MAP with:
- delivery dates for assets
- narrow usage restrictions (ephemeral, no derivative corpuses)
- acceptance criteria / runbooks
- schedule for takedown and confirmation of deletion

Also, is a short NDA addendum required for testcases? We can attach prompt_pack_v1.zip once legal signs.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call if easier.

—Sarah
Sarah Li
Head of ML Ops, OptiRetail

Hi Sarah —

Appreciate the note and the context. We can absolutely do a scoped MAP for an ephemeral evaluation. Outline below is my proposal — if you OK this, I’ll convert to a one‑page MAP doc and share with procurement.

Proposed MAP (high level):
1) Asset exchange
   - OptiRetail delivers: prompt_pack_v1.zip (<=150 cases, sanitized), metadata.csv (case ids + anonymization tags)
   - Redwood delivers: ingest_checklist.csv and a staging endpoint for run execution
2) Usage constraints
   - Ephemeral use only: test artifacts will not be used for training or model tuning
   - No indexing or persistent embedding storage; KV/prefix caching allowed for active session only
   - Audit logs preserved for 90 days; access records provided on request (CSV export)
3) Acceptance & eval cadence
   - Redwood runs 3x pass evaluation (baseline / normalization / final) over 7 business days and returns a results summary and raw run logs
   - Acceptance threshold: F1 >= 0.72 on slot extraction OR agreed sample-by-sample signoff
4) Takedown & certification
   - All copies removed within 10 business days after pilot close; Redwood will provide signed takedown certificate and a checksum of deleted artifacts
5) Timeline (draft)
   - Receive assets: Sep 29
   - Staging run window: Oct 4–12
   - Results & signoff: Oct 15

On the NDA: we don’t need a full NDA addendum for sanitized prompt packs but procurement frequently asks for a short MPA bullet covering data handling — I’ll prepare that.

If that looks good, I’ll circulate a one-page MAP + the ingest checklist and copy legal. Want to confirm: will you attach the prompt pack and the minimal metadata CSV on Sep 29?

Best —
Marissa Cole
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference

Quick technical notes on constraints / ingestion so legal gets accurate language: 

- We will accept the prompt pack as a ZIP with a single CSV/JSONL manifest. Please avoid any PII — if any rows contain customer-identifying data, we need explicit removal or tokenization.
- Ingest pipeline: data is staged on a dedicated ephemeral bucket with time-limited credentials; we’ll spin a dedicated job that does not persist embeddings to long-term storage.
- Audit artifacts: run logs (token counts, latency, per-case outputs) will be available as CSV and retained for 90 days as Marissa described.
- Access control: only the assigned engagement engineers (karthik_iyer, mina_haddad) and one legal contact will have access during the pilot.

If OptiRetail requires stricter guarantees (e.g., HSM-bound keys or additional isolation), flag that now and we’ll surface any operational cost impact.

—Karthik
Staff Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks, this looks good and aligns with procurement needs. Quick answers:

- No PII. If Karthik wants to validate, David can run a quick check prior to upload.
- We do not require HSM or special keys for this pilot — standard KMS with RBAC is fine.

Procurement note: Joe requests a one-page MAP and a short statement that Redwood will not use artifacts for training. Can you include the takedown certificate template in the MAP doc?

I’ll upload the ZIP to the shared Drive link you provided once legal signs.
